analysis.investment_thesis: Super Iron trades at a P/E of 25.4 with ROE of just 6.2% — the market is paying a growth multiple for a sub-mediocre capital return in a cyclical castings business. There is no margin of safety here by any Graham standard.
key_strengths: Established since 1988 with export-oriented casting operations
Small market cap (INR 66 Cr) leaves room if earnings normalize
key_risks: P/E of 25.4 is far above my <15 ceiling — speculative pricing
ROE 6.2% / ROCE 7.41% — returns below cost of capital
Cyclical foundry business vulnerable to commodity and demand swings
red_flags: P/E 25.4 with only 6.2% ROE implies ~4x book premium baked into price
Recent BSE listing — lacks the multi-year public earnings record I require
No disclosed dividend yield or current ratio — cannot verify balance sheet safety
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, Super Iron fails the most basic quantitative filters. A P/E of 25.4 paired with ROE of 6.2% is an outright contradiction — you are paying a premium multiple for a business earning less than a bank fixed deposit on its equity. ROCE of 7.41% does not cover any reasonable cost of capital for a cyclical, capital-intensive foundry. Without the book value, current ratio, debt/equity, interest coverage, or dividend history, I cannot even construct a Graham Number — and that absence itself is disqualifying. Castings & forgings is a commodity-exposed industry where earnings power must be demonstrated across a full cycle, not a single year.

The 70.88% promoter holding and long operating history since 1988 are mild positives, but neither compensates for valuation. Mr. Market is pricing this as a growth story; I see a small-cap cyclical with sub-par returns at a multiple reserved for compounders. The disciplined response is to wait — either for the price to collapse to a fraction of book with verified balance sheet strength, or for several consecutive years of demonstrably improved earnings power. At INR 44.30, this is speculation, not investment.
